title: Remote
summary: git remote manages the named addresses, like origin, that your repository pushes to and fetches from.

levels.title: Add a remote
levels.briefing: A remote is a short name for another repository's address. Cloning adds one called origin automatically; for a repository you started yourself, you add it with git remote add.
levels.objective: Connect this repository to https://example.com/team/notes.git under the name origin.
hints: git remote -v shows there are no remotes yet.
git remote add takes a name and an address.
Run: git remote add origin https://example.com/team/notes.git
levels.successMessage: origin is now a nickname for that address. Nothing was uploaded yet: that is what push does.

levels.title: A different name
levels.objective: Add https://example.com/team/notes.git as a remote called upstream.
hints: origin is only a convention. Any name works.
Run: git remote add upstream https://example.com/team/notes.git
levels.successMessage: A repository can have several remotes, each with its own name.

levels.title: Wrong address
levels.objective: origin points to the wrong address. Make it point to https://example.com/team/notes.git.
hints: git remote -v shows the wrong address.
Remove origin, then add it again with the right address.
Run: git remote remove origin, then git remote add origin https://example.com/team/notes.git
levels.successMessage: Removing and re-adding a remote only changes the nickname, not any files.

levels.title: Tidy up remotes
levels.objective: This repository has two remotes. Remove the one called old and keep origin.
hints: git remote remove takes the name to remove.
levels.successMessage: Only the old nickname is gone; origin is untouched.
